input: Submit my travel essay to a literary journal

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the essay is already written and polished, or still needs drafting or editing, completely changes what steps come first.
Understanding whether this is a first-ever submission or the user has submitted before determines how much guidance is needed on the submission process itself.
Whether the user already has a specific journal in mind or needs help identifying the right one shapes the entire research and targeting phase.
Submission deadlines, reading windows, or a target date for the user changes the urgency and sequencing of every step.
The essay's tone, style, and subject matter (e.g. personal memoir vs. reported travel writing) determines which journals are the best fit.
Whether the goal is simply to submit once, or to build a submission strategy across multiple journals, defines the scope of the plan.
Most journals require specific formatting, cover letters, and use submission platforms like Submittable — knowing what the user has already prepared avoids redundant steps.

gold.taskTitle: Submit travel essay to a literary journal
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to submit a completed (or in-progress) travel essay to one or more literary journals for publication consideration.

questions.title: Is your essay already written and ready to submit?
questions.description: Determine the current state of the essay — fully drafted and polished, drafted but needs editing, or still being written — to establish the correct starting point.

questions.title: Have you submitted to literary journals before?
questions.description: Establish the user's familiarity with the submission process to calibrate how much process guidance the plan should include.

questions.title: Do you have a specific journal in mind already?
questions.description: Find out if a target journal has been identified, or if the plan needs to include a journal research and shortlisting phase.

questions.title: Is there a submission deadline you are working toward?
questions.description: Identify any hard deadline, reading window close date, or personal target date that creates urgency in the plan.

questions.title: What is the style or tone of the essay?
questions.description: Understand whether the piece is personal memoir, lyric essay, reported travel narrative, or another form, so the right journals can be matched to it.

questions.title: Are you submitting to one journal or building a wider list?
questions.description: Clarify whether the goal is a single targeted submission or a simultaneous/sequential multi-journal strategy, which determines the breadth of the plan.

questions.title: Do you have a cover letter and formatted manuscript prepared?
questions.description: Check whether submission materials beyond the essay itself — cover letter, bio, formatting to guidelines, Submittable account — are already in place.
